Nations Championship: Dan Sheehan starts at No 8 for Ireland vs South Africa and Sam Prendergast plays after avoiding ban
Ireland hooker and captain Dan Sheehan has been shifted out of position to start at No 8 for the visit of South Africa to Dublin in Saturday's Nations Championship (4.40pm) in unusual and risky Andy Farrell move; Fly-half Sam Prendergast starts after citing against him dismissed
Thursday 19 November 2026 14:08, UK
Andy Farrell has named Dan Sheehan out of position at No 8 for Ireland's crunch Nations Championship Test against South Africa in Dublin on Saturday.
The unusual move, with Sheehan's ordinary position at hooker, comes with Ireland missing trio Caelan Doris, Jack Conan and Sean Jansen due to injury.
Sheehan has only played at No 8 once in his career to date, starting there for Leinster against Munster in last month's URC contest at the Aviva Stadium - a clash in which Leinster badly lost the breakdown battle before coming through to win.
Other changes see full-back Hugo Keenan, centre Robbie Henshaw and lock Joe McCarthy return to the squad to start.
Fly-half Sam Prendergast starts the contest after a citing against him for a hip-drop tackle was dismissed on Wednesday.
Wings Rob Baloucoune and Mack Hansen remain to form the back-three with Keenan, while Stuart McCloskey - who played most of last week's victory over Fiji off the bench - partners Henshaw in midfield.
Scrum-half Jamison Gibson-Park retains his starting place, with Craig Casey staying on the bench.
Into the forwards, Ronan Kelleher starts at hooker with Sheehan at No 8, while props Andrew Porter and Tadhg Furlong start either side of Kelleher in the front-row.
Tadhg Beirne starts again in the second row, alongside McCarthy, while Ryan Baird starts at blindside flanker and Josh van der Flier at openside ahead of Nick Timoney.
On the bench, replacement tighthead Sam Illo has been passed fit to be involved, while hooker Tom Stewart, loosehead Tom O'Toole, lock James Ryan, fly-half Ciaran Frawley and centre Bundee Aki complete the squad alongside Timoney and Casey.
Ireland squad to face South Africa in Nations Championship
Ireland: 15 Hugo Keenan, 14 Robert Baloucoune, 13 Robbie Henshaw, 12 Stuart McCloskey, 11 Mack Hansen, 10 Sam Prendergast, 9 Jamison Gibson-Park; 1 Andrew Porter, 2 Ronan Kelleher, 3 Tadhg Furlong, 4 Joe McCarthy, 5 Tadhg Beirne, 6 Ryan Baird, 7 Josh van der Flier, 8 Dan Sheehan (c).
Replacements: 16 Tom Stewart, 17 Tom O'Toole, 18 Sam Illo, 19 James Ryan, 20 Nick Timoney, 21 Craig Casey, 22 Ciaran Frawley, 23 Bundee Aki.
Springboks recall Etzebeth for crunch clash with Ireland in Dublin
For South Africa, they have recalled experienced lock Eben Etzebeth for the Nations Championship Test in Dublin, one of five changes to the starting XV that lost to France in Paris.
Etzebeth is set to extend his Springbok record to 148 caps by partnering Ruan Nortje in the second row, with Cameron Hanekom coming in at No 8 as Jasper Wiese serves a four-match suspension after his red card against the French.
Props Ox Nche and Wilco Louw plus hooker Malcolm Marx, who were originally selected as the front row last weekend before being replaced just before kick-off in a tactical switch, have been named in the starting XV again.
The backline remains the same with Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu at fly-half and Morne van den Berg the preferred scrum-half.
South Africa will likely need to beat Ireland to reach the Nations Championship final, although a losing bonus point could be enough if England defeat New Zealand and deny the All Blacks any bonus points.
"This is a massive match for us and we know the magnitude of facing Ireland in Dublin, so we felt it was important to strike a balance between consistency in selection, while managing some players and giving others who have been training hard and putting up their hands a chance in what will be a challenging encounter," coach Rassie Erasmus said.
Erasmus is now serving a six-Test suspension following extraordinary claims, saying "match-fixing" and "manipulation" was occurring in rugby.
South Africa: 15 Damian Willemse, 14 Kurt-Lee Arendse, 13 Jesse Kriel, 12 Damian de Allende, 11 Ethan Hooker, 10 Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, 9 Morne van den Berg; 1 Ox Nche, 2 Malcolm Marx, 3 Wilco Louw, 4 Eben Etzebeth, 5 Ruan Nortje, 6 Siya Kolisi (c), 7 Pieter-Steph du Toit, 8 Cameron Hanekom.
Replacements: 16 Jan-Hendrik Wessels, 17 Gerhard Steenekamp, 18 Thomas du Toit, 19 Lood de Jager, 20 Paul de Villiers, 21 Marco van Staden, 22 Grant Williams, 23 Canan Moodie.
digest_he:
מאמן נבחרת אירלנד, אנדי פארל, קיבל החלטה יוצאת דופן לקראת משחק הבית המכריע בגביע האומות מול דרום אפריקה בדבלין, והציב את הקוקר וקפטן הנבחרת דן שיאן בעמדת מספר 8 הלא שגרתית עבורו. המהלך נובע ממצוקת פציעות בנבחרת הכוללת את קאלן דוריס, ג'ק קונאן ושון ג'נסן. שיאן פתח בעמדה זו רק פעם אחת בעבר במדי קבוצת לנסטר. במקביל, הקשר סאם פנדרגאסט יפתח בהרכב לאחר שערעור שהוגש נגדו נדחה.

בצד המנוגד, נבחרת דרום אפריקה החזירה לסגל את הלוק הוותיק אבן אצבת, שצפוי לרשום את הופעתו ה-148 בנבחרת, וביצעה חמישה שינויים בהרכב הפותח בהשוואה למשחק ההפסד האחרון מול צרפת. קמרון האנקום יפתח בעמדת מספר 8 במקומו של ג'ספר ויזה המושעה. המאמן ראסי ארסמוס, המרצה בעצמו הרחקה, נדרש לאזן בין שמירה על רציפות מקצועית לבין ניהול הסגל לקראת התמודדות קשה ביותר מול האירים.
